The storage layer starts with three protocols; this is the first. ~Storage~ is the lifecycle contract (~initialize~ / ~close~) every backend implements, binding a concrete store to a ~DataSchema~ before any graph can be read or written.

* 5. MalliDataSchema
:PROPERTIES:

…and its ONE implementation. The record is an immutable bag of maps (~entities-map~, ~enums-map~, ~entity-uuids-map~, ~retired-fields-map~) with every protocol method a lookup into them — which is the point: a schema is data a builder assembled, not code. ~create-builder~ at the bottom of the file is what the ~:db/schema~ component calls, and the ~extend-builder~ fns below are how each subsystem contributes its entities to it.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/schema/malli/core.clj::(defrecord MalliDataSchema][src/graphden/schema/malli/core.clj:12]]

* 6. extend-builder
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: storage/extend-builder
:FILE: src/graphden/schema/graph/schema.clj
:LINE: 651
:MINS: 11.7
:END:

Where the graph model is actually declared: the ~ns~ / ~fn~ / ~slot~ / ~binding~ / ~binding-list-item~ entities and the ~:ref~ edges between them. This is the concrete table + foreign-key layout that every traversal walks.

Long, but it is one ~->~ pipeline rather than an algorithm: an ~add-entity~ per table with its fields inline, the ~add-constraint~ calls that become real UNIQUE indexes, and at the end the ~retire-field~ entries that keep dropped columns (~binding.rename-to~, ~fn.impl-hash~) from being resurrected. Skim it entity by entity — this is DDL that happens to be data.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/schema/graph/schema.clj::(defn extend-builder][src/graphden/schema/graph/schema.clj:651]]

* 13. PostgresStorage
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: storage/PostgresStorage
:FILE: src/graphden/storage/postgres/core.clj
:LINE: 134
:MINS: 10.3
:END:

The concrete Postgres backend. Its ~ExecutionGraph~ extension delegates to the Postgres resolver instead of the generic BFS — showing how a backend overrides the default path when it can do better.

Its length is protocol SURFACE, not logic: one record implementing ~Storage~, ~StorageIntrospection~, ~StorageCRUD~, the constraint protocols and ~ExecutionGraph~ in turn, most methods a single call deep. Read the protocol headings on the way down and stop at the ~ExecutionGraph~ arm — it is the only one doing something the generic path does not.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/storage/postgres/core.clj::(defrecord PostgresStorage][src/graphden/storage/postgres/core.clj:134]]

* 14. do-initialize
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: storage/do-initialize
:FILE: src/graphden/storage/postgres/migration.clj
:LINE: 297
:MINS: 3.2
:END:

Nobody hand-writes DDL here: the schema of the previous steps is DATA, and this diffs it against the metadata table to emit exactly the changes needed — first-init or migration, all in one transaction. Read the docstring for the fleet property that makes it safe: a transaction-scoped advisory lock taken BEFORE the state read, so N pods booting against one database serialize, and the second one computes a no-op instead of re-planning against pre-DDL state. This is why a graphden upgrade needs no DB reset (docs/OPERATIONS.md).

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/storage/postgres/migration.clj::(defn do-initialize][src/graphden/storage/postgres/migration.clj:297]]

* 15. reachable-fns-sql
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: storage/reachable-fns-sql
:FILE: src/graphden/storage/postgres/graph.clj
:LINE: 44
:MINS: 4.5
:END:

The ~WITH RECURSIVE~ CTE that walks every outgoing edge from the seed fn in one statement and returns the reachable ~fn.id~ set. This is the heart of the recursive-CTE traversal, mirroring in SQL exactly the edge list that ~process-fn-node~ computes in Clojure.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/storage/postgres/graph.clj::(def ^:private reachable-fns-sql][src/graphden/storage/postgres/graph.clj:44]]

* 16. resolve-execution-graph
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: storage/resolve-execution-graph~2
:FILE: src/graphden/storage/postgres/graph.clj
:LINE: 118
:MINS: 4.7

The optimized resolver: run the CTE to get reachable ids, enforce the graph-size cap, bulk-load fn / slot / binding rows with five ~IN~-clause queries, and hand off to ~->execution-graph~. O(1) round-trips versus the generic O(N) — the payoff of the whole protocol split.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/storage/postgres/graph.clj::(defn resolve-execution-graph][src/graphden/storage/postgres/graph.clj:118]]

* 17. make-emitter
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: storage/make-emitter
:FILE: src/graphden/storage/postgres/notify.clj
:LINE: 304
:MINS: 2.1
:END:

How a committed write reaches every OTHER pod. The emitter is a closure over the pooled DataSource that sends one ~pg_notify~ on ~graphden_events~; best-effort by design — a NOTIFY failure must never roll back a row-level write, because the mutation-driven reconcile is the correctness path and NOTIFY only makes propagation fast. ~notify-after-write!~ in the CRUD block is its caller.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/storage/postgres/notify.clj::(defn make-emitter][src/graphden/storage/postgres/notify.clj:304]]
- see also :: [[file:crud.org::#crud/notify-after-write!][notify-after-write!]]

* 18. create-listener
:PROPERTIES:
:CUSTOM_ID: storage/create-listener
:FILE: src/graphden/storage/postgres/notify.clj
:LINE: 244
:MINS: 2.4
:END:

The receiving end: one DEDICATED connection (outside the pool — LISTEN is session state) subscribed to ~graphden_events~, a background poll thread, reconnect with backoff, and a callback set that ~register!~ / ~unregister!~ mutate. Callback exceptions are isolated so one bad listener cannot silence the rest. The branch router's invalidation, the reconciler and the SSE panels all hang off this handle.

- source :: [[file:../../../src/graphden/storage/postgres/notify.clj::(defn create-listener][src/graphden/storage/postgres/notify.clj:244]]
